T.topic_fa: مک‌دونالد این کریسمس به بچه‌ها نمی‌فروشد؛ کوین «تنها در خانه» را ۳۶ سال بعد برگرداند تا به بزرگ‌ترها کودکیِ خودشان را بفروشد
T.topic_en: McDonald's brought back Home Alone's Kevin 36 years later. The ad isn't for kids: it sells grown-ups the child they used to be
T.central_tension_fa: همه فکر می‌کنند فست‌فود برای بچه‌ها تبلیغ می‌کند؛ ولی بزرگ‌ترین تبلیغ کریسمس مک‌دونالد برای آدم‌های چهل‌ساله است. تیتر خودشان: «بزرگ‌سالی را پشت سر بگذار». محصول برگر نیست؛ برگشتن به ده‌سالگی است، و جوراب یادگاری رسیدِ این سفر است.
T.central_tension_en: Everyone assumes fast food advertises to kids. McDonald's biggest Christmas ad is aimed at forty-year-olds; its own headline says 'Leave Adulthood Behind'. The product isn't the burger. It's a trip back to being ten, and the collectible socks are the souvenir.
T.working_hook_fa: مک‌دونالد کوینِ «تنها در خانه» را برگرداند. ولی این تبلیغ برای بچه‌ها نیست؛ برای شماست.
T.working_hook_en: McDonald's just brought Kevin back. This ad isn't for kids. It's for the kid you were.

T.framing_note: Type 2. Spine: (1) Kevin is back, alone in a closed McDonald's on Christmas, 36 years later; (2) the twist: look who it's for - the release literally says 'Leave Adulthood Behind'; (3) why: adults are the new Happy Meal customer (McDonaldland adult meal, Minecraft meal) - nostalgia lets a grown-up buy back a feeling; (4) the souvenir: socks, a cheap object that makes the memory physical and collectible; (5) lesson: find the memory your customer already owns and give them a door back into it. One number on screen: 36 (years). Music: 'dark' per rule (strategy angle), keep it warm-dark, not horror. DO NOT: show Macaulay Culkin's face or any frame of him (public figure photo rule) - use the meal, socks and fries packshots only; reproduce the Home Alone 'scream' pose or film stills/characters; AI-generate McDonald's arches or the Home Alone logo; say it is viral by numbers (no counts exist); use the '7 weeks after vowing own IP' claim (single paraphrased source, contradicted by Adweek); repeat yesterday's 'fictional brand made real' angle (Little Nero's fries: mention at most as a detail). Availability differs by market (US Dec 1): never imply it's on sale everywhere. Caption: sources + 'editorial use; images belong to their owners'. Never name the UAE, Dubai or any emirate.
